messages.author: fc1ebff267fb2384
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] plots not rendering when fig.* options added to an R chunk
parts:
I don't understand what's going on, but I believe it has something to do with knitr getting confused by out.width. Consider this very minimal example, free from rmarkdown/Rstudio interaction,

> knit(text = "```{r test}
+      plot(1,1)
+      ```")
  |.................................................................| 100%
label: test

[1] " ```r     plot(1,1) ``` ![plot of chunk test](figure/test.png) "
> knit(text = "```{r test, out.width=''}
+      plot(1,1)
+      ```")
  |.................................................................| 100%
label: test (with options) 
List of 1
 $ out.width: chr ""


[1] " ```r     plot(1,1) ``` <img src=\"figure/test.png\" title=\"plot of chunk test\" alt=\"plot of chunk test\" width=\"\" />"

out.width seems to trigger a switch to html in the output format, which might subsequently get stripped by rmarkdown in your tex workflow?

Cheers,

baptiste

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] plots not rendering when fig.* options added to an R chunk
parts:
I think Baptiste provided the correct answer. At the moment, there are
four chunk options that you should not use for plot chunks in R
Markdown documents when you expect the final output to be
LaTeX/PDF/Word: out.width, out.height, fig.center, and out.extra. The
reason is that there is no way to specify image width, height, or
alignment in Markdown syntax. If you do specify these options, knitr
has to turn to the HTML syntax <img>, which only works for HTML output
but not LaTeX/Word.

I intended to fix this but has not managed to find some time yet.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] plots not rendering when fig.* options added to an R chunk
parts:
Oh, sorry, yes, I mean fig.align.

As I said, I will put the LaTeX benefits back in Markdown, which is
possible but I have not done yet. If you want figure captions (i.e.
the figure environments), you need

output:
html_document:
fig_caption: yes

in the YAML metadata. This is more obvious if you use RStudio, which
has a gear button to set these options on the toolbar. The less
obvious way is to read the documentation of rmarkdown::html_document
to know what the possible options are.

Regards,
Yihui
--
